items.item_text: Current Central Service Certification or Scrub Technician background and/or equivalent experience and training.
Experience in Sterile Processing with a proven track record in sterile processing clinical operations, clinical programs development, planning, and process

Play a key role in the delivery of world-class patient care. Continuously elevate the quality of care within an award-winning health system. Leverage your expertise to make a real difference in others’ lives.

The Ambulatory Medical Device Reprocessing Specialist (MDRS), provides operational improvement support to the UCLA Health Ambulatory Services by functioning, as necessary, as a high-level disinfection and sterilization educator, facilitator, consultant, and analyst. The MDRS designs and facilitates improvement efforts by incorporating best practices based on evidence, and by analyzing various accumulations of data to assist ambulatory management at each clinical site with information pertaining to instrumentation and equipment decisions related to both the operating and capital budgets. You will demonstrate the ability to analyze, design and communicate complex issues related to high level disinfection and sterilization including standardized processes, logistics, identify regulatory deficiencies and develop solutions for compliance.
Basic understanding of Quality Management and Performance Improvement programs.
Able to work independently with minimal supervision.

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Computer and data entry skills required: knowledge of Word, Excel, Access, and Outlook.
Knowledgeable of healthcare regulations for infection prevention & control.
Excellent customer service and time management skills.
Team player and ability to work well under pressure.
